name: SkillOpt
institution: Microsoft Research (authors: Yifan Yang, Ziyang Gong, Weiquan Huang, Qihao Yang, Ziwei Zhou, Zisu Huang, Yan Li, Xuemei Gao, Qi Dai, Bei Liu, Kai Qiu, Yuqing Yang, Dongdong Chen, Xue Yang, Chong Luo)
release_date: 2026-05-22 (arXiv v1; v2 on 2026-05-25); PyPI v0.1.0 on 2026-06-02; SkillOpt-Sleep preview on 2026-06-15
type: academic (paper) with open-source framework (MIT license, pip install skillopt)
what_evolved: Context memory / prompt — a compact natural-language skill document is treated as the trainable external state of a frozen LLM agent; model weights are NOT updated. (category: skill_library)
skill_as_artifact: Yes — a single deployable best_skill.md (open SKILL.md format, ~300–2,000 tokens) that runs against the unchanged target model; reusable/transferable across models, harnesses, and nearby benchmarks; adds zero inference-time optimizer calls at deployment
skill_encoding: Skill document (.md, SKILL.md format) — natural-language procedural instructions (no executable code, no vectors)
skill_granularity: 策略规则 / 子任务workflow — a procedural skill document (strategic rules, heuristics, and sub-task procedures)
how_method: rollout_optimization (non-gradient, text-space optimization). Mirrors weight-space SGD discipline: the frozen target model runs scored rollouts (forward pass), a SEPARATE optimizer model reflects on success/failure minibatches and proposes bounded add/delete/replace edits, an edit is accepted only if it strictly improves held-out validation. Uses epochs, (mini-)batch size, textual learning-rate budget, rejected-edit buffer, and epoch-wise slow/meta update. Non-gradient.
learning_signal_source: 成败轨迹 (scored rollout trajectories: messages, tool calls, verifier feedback, task metadata, final scores) + optimizer-side reflection (success and failure minibatches reflected separately by the optimizer model) + held-out validation score as gate
reward_granularity: hybrid — outcome (final task score / held-out validation score as acceptance gate) combined with process evidence (per-example rollout trajectory analysis by optimizer)
learning_paradigm: online, on-policy — fresh rollouts are collected each epoch by the target model with the current skill; offline SkillOpt-Sleep companion runs nightly replay over past sessions
when_evolve: inter-test-time (offline training phase before deployment; a nightly offline self-evolution companion 'SkillOpt-Sleep' consolidates validated skills behind a held-out gate)
trigger: 周期性 (epoch-driven training loop with held-out selection); SkillOpt-Sleep event-based (reviews past sessions / recurring tasks nightly)
library_structure: 技能文件 — optimizes a SINGLE skill document per benchmark/domain (best_skill.md), not a multi-skill vector/graph library; one skill file per run
retrieval_method: [uncertain] No retrieval mechanism — a single skill file is loaded directly as agent context per domain; skill artifacts are transferred (not retrieved) across model scales, harnesses, and nearby benchmarks. Closest option: direct injection / artifact transfer rather than semantic or generative retrieval
validation: validation gating — a candidate edit is accepted ONLY when it strictly improves a held-out validation score (selection-best checkpoint), turning reflection into propose-and-test optimization rather than unconditional self-editing; execution-based benchmark scores
error_correction: 有界编辑 (bounded add/delete/replace edits under a textual learning-rate budget preventing destructive rewrites) + rejected-edit buffer (rejected edits stored as negative feedback so the optimizer avoids repeating harmful directions) + epoch-wise slow/meta update (rescues useful-but-skipped edits, longer-horizon memory without bloating deployment)
test_env: general / multi-domain across six benchmarks — SearchQA, SpreadsheetBench, OfficeQA, DocVQA, LiveMath (LiveMathBench), ALFWorld (embodied text-world); three execution harnesses: direct chat, Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI
backbone_model: Frozen target models: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini, GPT-5.4-nano, GPT-5.2, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B; separate optimizer model (e.g., GPT-5.5; also works with matched target-as-optimizer); multi-backend support OpenAI / Azure / Claude / Qwen / MiniMax
where_deploy: general — multi-domain; deployed as a compact best_skill.md inside coding agents (Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, Copilot) and direct chat
metrics: success_rate (task accuracy), generalization (cross-model / cross-harness / cross-benchmark transfer), cost (zero inference-time optimizer calls), ablation accuracy, per-cell comparison vs baselines
key_results: Best or tied-best on ALL 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells; on GPT-5.5 lifts average no-skill accuracy by +23.5pt (direct chat), +24.8pt (Codex loop), +19.1pt (Claude Code); beats human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, and EvoSkill skills on every benchmark; ALFWorld test-hard 70.9%→85.8%; transfer +15.2pt cross-model, +31.8pt cross-harness (Codex→Claude Code), +10.4pt self-optimizer; ablations show textual learning rate, rejected-edit buffer, and slow/meta update each contribute gains
limitations: scalability — optimizes a single skill document per run, not a full multi-skill library (no retrieval/indexing); requires task-level verifier / scored rollouts (needs environment feedback); gains depend on optimizer-model quality (though self-optimizer setting still works); training compute cost for repeated rollouts; controllability, catastrophic-forgetting, and eval-hacking are explicitly MITIGATED via bounded edits + held-out gate + buffer (strengths rather than weaknesses)
